A time panel under the map: one group's rows over time, linked to the map

Source: R/time.R
rr_time.Rd

rr_time() adds a panel under a map, or starts a map with it, that shows one group's rows over time (a vessel's, a float's, an animal's: the values of by):

  • a column or several as lines, the first shown and the others ticked on in the panel;

  • marks where a column says so (a flag), on the chart and on the map;

  • lanes of intervals under the chart (visits, legs, phases), a click on one setting the window to it.

Usage

rr_time(
  x,
  col,
  marks = NULL,
  lanes = NULL,
  span = NULL,
  max_gap_s = NULL,
  span_max = 3e+06,
  time_label = "UTC",
  data = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  title = "Track",
  port = 8790L
)

Arguments

x

Rows: a data frame or lazy DuckDB table with lon and lat (WGS 84), or an sf object of points; or a map, whose rows, time and group (from rr_path()) the panel takes.

col

The numeric columns drawn over time, a name, a string or c() of them; the first shown.

marks

Columns that mark rows, as col: a logical column marks its TRUE rows, any other its values that are not missing (such as a flag's label). Each column is a row of ticks along the chart's top and a ring on the map in a colour of its own, named in the sidebar; c(truth = "wrong", clean = "flag") names them.

lanes

Intervals drawn as lanes under the chart: a named list (the names are the lanes' labels), each

  • a column of the rows, as a string: its runs of one value (a phase, a leg), missing values left out and a run broken by a silence longer than max_gap_s;

  • a table of intervals with the group's column (by), and its start and end in start and end;

  • or list(data = , start = , end = , label = ), naming the columns, label a column that names each interval.

span

Units the page holds one at a time, chosen besides the whole series: a column of the rows that names them, as a string (a leg, a deployment: "leg", or c(leg = "leg_id") to name the list), one span per value from its first row to its last; or a table of intervals, or list(data = , start = , end = , label = ), as for lanes, named as a column is with list(legs = <table>). A span holds every row of its group from its start to its end, those whose value is missing too. Spans that overlap are reported: a state that comes and goes, such as behaviour, belongs in lanes. NULL, the default, offers the whole series alone.

max_gap_s

A silence between two rows longer than this many seconds breaks the panel's line, on the chart and on the map, and a lane's run of one value. By default a path's (rr_path()'s max_gap_s) when the map has one already, else Inf: nothing broken, so no gap is hidden.

span_max

The most rows the page holds at once: a group with more is offered by its spans, else by month. The browser holds far more than the default is likely to meet: a series of 2.2 million rows loaded in about 8 seconds, most of it the transfer.

time_label

The clock the times are on, shown beside them.

data

Rows for this panel, in place of the map's.

lon, lat, time

The position and time columns: by default the map's, else "lon", "lat" and "time".

by

The column whose values each have a series, a name or a string: by default the map's (a path's group), else one series of all the rows.

title, port

The page's title, and where the map is served when printed: set by the call that starts it.

Value

An rr_map() with the time panel.

Details

The panel and the map are linked. A drag across the chart sets the time window, and a double click goes back to the whole span. The map draws the window's path and points, and fits to them. A hover on the chart marks that row on the map, and a click on a point of the window marks its time on the chart. The group, the span and the window go into the page's address.

The page holds one group's span at a time: by default its whole series; with span, also each of its intervals, chosen under Span. A group with more than span_max rows is offered by its spans only, or by month where there are none. The map's other layers that carry the group and a time (rr_path(), rr_point()) show only the chosen group and span; a path's line that runs over a span's start or end is shown whole. The window's path is drawn whole, its points thinned to about 5,000 (every k-th, a marked one always), so the map stays quick.

Times are shown as the data hold them, in no time zone, labelled by time_label.

See also

rr_path() and rr_point(), the layers it pairs with; rr_bundle(), which writes the panel's series beside the page.

Examples

# \donttest{
d <- dplyr::filter(dplyr::collect(rr_example("dansk")), vessel_id %in% c("EX_1", "EX_12"))
m <- rr_map(d) |>
  rr_path(group = vessel_id, time = time_stamp) |>
  rr_time(speed, lanes = list(behaviour = "behaviour"))
format(m)
#> [1] "<rr_map> Map"                                             
#> [2] "  layers: paths (vector)"                                 
#> [3] "  time panel: speed over time, 2 groups; lanes: behaviour"
# m  # printed at the console, the map opens with the panel under it
# }
